## Overview

Fuse the Gemma add+RMSNorm in front of an AITER asm MXFP4 GEMM into the GEMM's activation quant (one kernel instead of a norm kernel plus a separate HIP quant kernel), opt-in on gfx950, for the two norms of a decoder layer: the post-attention norm that feeds the MLP's gate_up (`VLLM_ROCM_AITER_FP4_POSTNORM_QUANT_FUSION`) and the input norm that starts the layer (`VLLM_ROCM_AITER_FP4_INPUTNORM_QUANT_FUSION`). An input norm whose output feeds two GEMMs (a gated delta net layer: `in_proj_qkvz` and `in_proj_ba`) is quantized once, and both GEMMs take the same codes and scales; the GEMMs quantized the same tensor twice before. Builds on #59153 (its commit is the first commit of this PR, unchanged); the PR also puts that pass behind an env flag and adds a start-up check that a fusion flag that is on really rewrote the target model.

Not a duplicate: #59153 fuses the activation (SiLU/GELU+Mul) before the down projection on the same asm path; #59610 folds RMSNorm and SiLU+Mul into the MXFP4 quant on the Triton `afp4wfp4` path with `fused_rms_mxfp4_quant` (plain RMSNorm, measured on Llama-3.1-8B); #59483 and #59553 fuse the quant into AR+RMSNorm and into the GDN gated RMSNorm. This PR adds the add+Gemma-RMSNorm into the asm GEMM, with AITER's `add_rmsnorm_quant`. The files overlap with #59610 (`mxfp4/aiter.py`, `rocm_aiter_fusion.py`, `_aiter_ops.py`); both PRs conflict with #59153 in `mxfp4/aiter.py` in the same place, and I will rebase on whichever lands first.

## Claims

- On gfx950 with `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_FP4_POSTNORM_QUANT_FUSION=1`, each post-attention add+RMSNorm that feeds an asm MXFP4 GEMM becomes one AITER kernel (add, Gemma norm, MXFP4 quant). Fused kernels per target forward on Qwen3.8-27B: 64 sites (start-up log, `graph=backbone`). In a torch profile, standalone quant launches per target forward pass go from 304 to 240 (post-attention flag alone; 274 of 274 passes at c=1 and 233 of 233 at c=64, against 304 on every pass of the control).
- With `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_FP4_INPUTNORM_QUANT_FUSION=1`, the same for each decoder layer's input norm; a norm that feeds two GEMMs is one fused kernel and the GEMMs' own quant kernels are gone. Fused kernels per target forward: 63 sites (start-up log, `graph=backbone`, both norm flags on). Standalone quant launches per target forward pass: 304 with no flag, 240 with the post-attention flag, 130 with both norm flags (282 of 282 passes at c=1, 234 of 234 at c=64). Adding #59153's act fusion: 66 (second card of the same host, own control at 304). The input flag alone: Not measured.
- End to end on Qwen3.8-27B MXFP4, MI350P (gfx950, 128 CU, 450 W power cap), MTP 2, this change backported onto the image under Validation. Both norm flags against none, decode at T=0: +2.2% at c=1 (184.9 to 188.9 tok/s). That gain is outside the run-to-run spread (the difference of the means, 4.0 tok/s, is larger than the max-min spread of the control's 3 runs, 1.0 tok/s), and the profile explains it (GPU kernel time per target pass 11.693 ms to 11.133 ms, -4.8%). At c=8, 16, 32 and 64 the change is +1.4% to +3.3% (+2.2% at c=64, 3509.8 to 3586.3 tok/s), which is inside the spread of the control's runs (17.0, 117.7, 92.8 and 104.7 tok/s at c=8, 16, 32 and 64), so no gain is claimed there; at c=64 the profile shows no GPU time saved (24.101 ms to 24.168 ms). Time to first token 1.6% to 3.3% faster at 3000 to 16384 input tokens. The post-attention flag alone: -0.6% to +1.4% at T=0. With #59153's act fusion also on (second card, own control): T=0 c=1 +3.0% (5.4 tok/s against a control spread of 0.7), c=8 +2.9% (31.0 against 4.0) and c=32 +2.5% (66.6 against 51.3) are larger than the control's spread; c=16 +3.5% (60.7 against 66.7) and c=64 -0.2% are not. Time to first token 3.0% to 4.2% faster. Tables under Validation.
- Accuracy, both norm flags against none: GSM8K on all 1319 questions, 5-shot, T=1.0: 92.42 against 93.10 (flexible-extract), 92.87 against 93.10 (strict-match), not significant (McNemar exact p=0.4519 for flexible-extract and 0.8468 for strict-match). json_schema, 60 requests: 60/60 against 60/60. At T=0 the output is not bit-identical to the unfused path (0 of 50 prompts identical over 200 tokens). With #59153's act fusion also on (measured on the first card, against that card's control of 93.10): GSM8K 92.57 (flexible-extract) and 93.18 (strict-match), json_schema 58/60 (the 2 failures hit the length limit, the control has none). A larger json_schema check on the second card, 5 runs of 60 requests per arm against that card's own control (T=1.0, `max_tokens` 4000, 8 at a time), found no significant difference: 8 of 300 requests ended at the length limit for the control, 5 of 300 with the two norm flags and 11 of 300 with the act fusion also on (Fisher exact test on the length-limit count, two-sided, p 0.58 and 0.64); 292, 294 and 289 of 300 replies were valid JSON that matches the schema. Replies that were invalid without ending at the length limit: 0 for the control, 1 for the two norm flags (empty content, finish=stop) and 0 with the act fusion. The 2 length-limit failures of the 60-request check above are within that spread. I run the act fusion in my own serving setup (all three flags on).
- Nothing changes with the flags unset (all three default off, and a flag also needs the matching `fuse_*` pass config switch and a gfx950).

## Validation

Tests (new files and additions; `test_rocm_aiter_act_mul_mxfp4_fusion.py` is #59153's own test file, carried as this PR's first commit; the GPU rows are run on a gfx950, the others run anywhere):

```bash
pytest tests/compile/passes/test_rocm_aiter_mxfp4_fusion_gating.py \
       tests/compile/passes/test_rocm_aiter_mxfp4_norm_fusion.py \
       tests/compile/passes/test_vllm_fusion_pattern_matcher_pass.py \
       tests/compile/passes/test_rocm_aiter_act_mul_mxfp4_fusion.py \
       tests/kernels/test_rocm_aiter_rmsnorm_mxfp4_quant.py -v
```

## Details

**The fusion.** On the asm path the MXFP4 linear quantizes its input inside the `gemm_with_dynamic_quant` custom op, so Inductor cannot fuse the norm into it. The new op `rocm_aiter_rmsnorm_mxfp4_quant(x, residual, weight, epsilon)` calls AITER's `add_rmsnorm_quant` and returns the MXFP4 codes, the shuffled e8m0 scales and the residual output; the GEMM takes the codes and scales through its existing `x_scales` argument. The pass `RocmAiterRMSNormMxfp4GemmFusionPass` rewrites `fused_add_rms_norm -> gemm_with_dynamic_quant` (asm path) into the op plus that GEMM(s). It is built once per enabled flag: `sites="post"` takes the post-attention norm of each decoder layer (one GEMM, gate_up), `sites="input"` takes the input norm that starts a layer, so each flag is judged and logged on its own and both flags together give two passes. The two kinds look the same by shape; the pass tells them apart by where the residual comes from, which needs the graph split at the attention ops, and refuses to be built without that split.

**The shared quantization.** An input norm feeds one GEMM in a full-attention layer (`qkv_proj`) and two in a gated delta net layer (`in_proj_qkvz`, `in_proj_ba`). The pattern matcher cannot match a norm whose output has users beyond the pattern's, so the input pass registers a second pattern, `AiterAddRMSNormMxfp4GemmPairPattern`, for two GEMMs: one fused op, and both GEMMs take its codes and scales through `x_scales`. A site is fused for all of its consumers or for none: a norm with a third GEMM, a reader that is not a GEMM, or one GEMM that is ineligible (below) is left whole. The pair pattern has two GEMM slots; the matcher can bind both to the same GEMM depending on the order in which the graph lists the users, so `extra_check` refuses that match and the matcher goes on to the real pair (a test lists the users both ways). The pass uuid includes the site kind, so the compile cache never serves one kind's graph for the other.

**What the pass refuses, at match time** (the op's fake raises on what it cannot take, so these must not reach it): tensor parallel size above 1, hidden size not a multiple of 32 or above 8192, non-bf16 or non-2D inputs, and a GEMM weight shape (of any GEMM of the site) with a tuned Triton preshuffle config (that GEMM may take a small-M branch that reads unshuffled scales; the op writes the asm layout). The op's argument contract is one pure function, `rocm_aiter_rmsnorm_mxfp4_quant_args_error`, used by the op, its fake and the pass.

**Start-up check.** `TargetGraphSiteCheckMixin` counts rewritten sites per compile range (the first piece of a model has no site, so nothing is judged per piece). `PostGradPassManager.finish_compile`, called by `VllmBackend` after the last piece and before the compile cache index is saved, makes the pass judge the whole graph: a target model graph in which the pass ran for a compile range and rewrote nothing fails the start, naming the flag; speculative decoding graphs (`is_target_model_graph`, e.g. the bf16 MTP head) are only logged. If the pass never ran because Inductor served every piece from its cache, a warning is logged. The backend hands the graph name to the pass manager as an attribute and calls `finish_compile` only if the pass manager has it, so a platform's own pass manager (`get_pass_manager_cls`) keeps working unchanged. N in the log line counts the sites in the pieces the pass ran on; vLLM compiles identical pieces once.

**Small shared changes.** `VllmPatternReplacement.extra_check` (default accepts everything) is forwarded by `VllmFusionPatternMatcherPass.register`, so a replacement can refuse a match; existing replacements are unaffected. The fake of `gemm_with_dynamic_quant` takes its arguments in the real op's order (already in #59153; a test pins it, because passing `x_scales` and `out_dtype` positionally depends on it).

**Limits.** gfx950 asm MXFP4 path only; tensor parallel 1; Gemma-style norm (the kernel adds 1 to the weight). Not covered: the gated RMSNorm inside a gated delta net (the subject of #59553), and layer 0's norm, which is a plain `rms_norm` with no residual. Size: about 820 lines of source on top of #59153 (the op and its contract 180, the passes and the start-up check 555, wiring and flags 86) and about 2650 lines of tests, most of them on fake tensors; I can split it: the op and its contract, then the post-attention pass and the start-up check, then the input pass and the pair pattern. Expected to work on any gfx950 (MI350X, MI355X, MI350P); tested only on MI350P (128 CU). On 256-CU parts, AITER's shipped tuned tables route some GEMM shapes to the Triton preshuffle path, which the pass refuses, so fewer sites may fuse there. Open PRs that would change these figures if they land first: #58139 routes 96-row scale tiles (the GDN `in_proj_ba` GEMM) to Triton, so the 47 GDN input-norm sites would stay unfused and the 63-site and launch-count figures would drop; #61278 removes `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4_ASM_GEMM`, which the commands above set. I will update this PR if either merges first.

detail.body:
## Overview

Fuse the Gemma add+RMSNorm in front of an AITER asm MXFP4 GEMM into the GEMM's activation quant (one kernel instead of a norm kernel plus a separate HIP quant kernel), opt-in on gfx950, for the two norms of a decoder layer: the post-attention norm that feeds the MLP's gate_up (`VLLM_ROCM_AITER_FP4_POSTNORM_QUANT_FUSION`) and the input norm that starts the layer (`VLLM_ROCM_AITER_FP4_INPUTNORM_QUANT_FUSION`). An input norm whose output feeds two GEMMs (a gated delta net layer: `in_proj_qkvz` and `in_proj_ba`) is quantized once, and both GEMMs take the same codes and scales; the GEMMs quantized the same tensor twice before. Builds on #59153 (its commit is the first commit of this PR, unchanged); the PR also puts that pass behind an env flag and adds a start-up check that a fusion flag that is on really rewrote the target model.

Not a duplicate: #59153 fuses the activation (SiLU/GELU+Mul) before the down projection on the same asm path; #59610 folds RMSNorm and SiLU+Mul into the MXFP4 quant on the Triton `afp4wfp4` path with `fused_rms_mxfp4_quant` (plain RMSNorm, measured on Llama-3.1-8B); #59483 and #59553 fuse the quant into AR+RMSNorm and into the GDN gated RMSNorm. This PR adds the add+Gemma-RMSNorm into the asm GEMM, with AITER's `add_rmsnorm_quant`. The files overlap with #59610 (`mxfp4/aiter.py`, `rocm_aiter_fusion.py`, `_aiter_ops.py`); both PRs conflict with #59153 in `mxfp4/aiter.py` in the same place, and I will rebase on whichever lands first.

## Claims

- On gfx950 with `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_FP4_POSTNORM_QUANT_FUSION=1`, each post-attention add+RMSNorm that feeds an asm MXFP4 GEMM becomes one AITER kernel (add, Gemma norm, MXFP4 quant). Fused kernels per target forward on Qwen3.8-27B: 64 sites (start-up log, `graph=backbone`). In a torch profile, standalone quant launches per target forward pass go from 304 to 240 (post-attention flag alone; 274 of 274 passes at c=1 and 233 of 233 at c=64, against 304 on every pass of the control).
- With `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_FP4_INPUTNORM_QUANT_FUSION=1`, the same for each decoder layer's input norm; a norm that feeds two GEMMs is one fused kernel and the GEMMs' own quant kernels are gone. Fused kernels per target forward: 63 sites (start-up log, `graph=backbone`, both norm flags on). Standalone quant launches per target forward pass: 304 with no flag, 240 with the post-attention flag, 130 with both norm flags (282 of 282 passes at c=1, 234 of 234 at c=64). Adding #59153's act fusion: 66 (second card of the same host, own control at 304). The input flag alone: Not measured.
- End to end on Qwen3.8-27B MXFP4, MI350P (gfx950, 128 CU, 450 W power cap), MTP 2, this change backported onto the image under Validation. Both norm flags against none, decode at T=0: +2.2% at c=1 (184.9 to 188.9 tok/s). That gain is outside the run-to-run spread (the difference of the means, 4.0 tok/s, is larger than the max-min spread of the control's 3 runs, 1.0 tok/s), and the profile explains it (GPU kernel time per target pass 11.693 ms to 11.133 ms, -4.8%). At c=8, 16, 32 and 64 the change is +1.4% to +3.3% (+2.2% at c=64, 3509.8 to 3586.3 tok/s), which is inside the spread of the control's runs (17.0, 117.7, 92.8 and 104.7 tok/s at c=8, 16, 32 and 64), so no gain is claimed there; at c=64 the profile shows no GPU time saved (24.101 ms to 24.168 ms). Time to first token 1.6% to 3.3% faster at 3000 to 16384 input tokens. The post-attention flag alone: -0.6% to +1.4% at T=0. With #59153's act fusion also on (second card, own control): T=0 c=1 +3.0% (5.4 tok/s against a control spread of 0.7), c=8 +2.9% (31.0 against 4.0) and c=32 +2.5% (66.6 against 51.3) are larger than the control's spread; c=16 +3.5% (60.7 against 66.7) and c=64 -0.2% are not. Time to first token 3.0% to 4.2% faster. Tables under Validation.
- Accuracy, both norm flags against none: GSM8K on all 1319 questions, 5-shot, T=1.0: 92.42 against 93.10 (flexible-extract), 92.87 against 93.10 (strict-match), not significant (McNemar exact p=0.4519 for flexible-extract and 0.8468 for strict-match). json_schema, 60 requests: 60/60 against 60/60. At T=0 the output is not bit-identical to the unfused path (0 of 50 prompts identical over 200 tokens). With #59153's act fusion also on (measured on the first card, against that card's control of 93.10): GSM8K 92.57 (flexible-extract) and 93.18 (strict-match), json_schema 58/60 (the 2 failures hit the length limit, the control has none). A larger json_schema check on the second card, 5 runs of 60 requests per arm against that card's own control (T=1.0, `max_tokens` 4000, 8 at a time), found no significant difference: 8 of 300 requests ended at the length limit for the control, 5 of 300 with the two norm flags and 11 of 300 with the act fusion also on (Fisher exact test on the length-limit count, two-sided, p 0.58 and 0.64); 292, 294 and 289 of 300 replies were valid JSON that matches the schema. Replies that were invalid without ending at the length limit: 0 for the control, 1 for the two norm flags (empty content, finish=stop) and 0 with the act fusion. The 2 length-limit failures of the 60-request check above are within that spread. I run the act fusion in my own serving setup (all three flags on).
- Nothing changes with the flags unset (all three default off, and a flag also needs the matching `fuse_*` pass config switch and a gfx950).

## Validation

Tests (new files and additions; `test_rocm_aiter_act_mul_mxfp4_fusion.py` is #59153's own test file, carried as this PR's first commit; the GPU rows are run on a gfx950, the others run anywhere):

```bash
pytest tests/compile/passes/test_rocm_aiter_mxfp4_fusion_gating.py \
       tests/compile/passes/test_rocm_aiter_mxfp4_norm_fusion.py \
       tests/compile/passes/test_vllm_fusion_pattern_matcher_pass.py \
       tests/compile/passes/test_rocm_aiter_act_mul_mxfp4_fusion.py \
       tests/kernels/test_rocm_aiter_rmsnorm_mxfp4_quant.py -v
```

| Run | Result |

| Fake-tensor and CPU-runnable tests (flags, gating, site check, op contract, pass rewrites of both site kinds on toy graphs, base-class hook) on a CPU container built from the pinned image (not a vLLM main build) with ROCm and AITER emulated | 170 passed, 24 skipped (the skips need a gfx950 GPU or a CUDA-class GPU); #59153's own 24 GPU cases are deselected in this row (they need a real GPU), so it covers 194 of the 218 cases of the five files |
| Same files on plain CPU, no ROCm, in the same pinned-image container | 50 passed, 168 skipped (the ROCm-only tests skip) |
| gfx950, real platform and real AITER: `rocm_aiter_rmsnorm_mxfp4_quant` against the AITER kernel, rewritten graph against unrewritten graph (post-attention site, input pair), real act+quant pass, and the other tests of the files in the command above | 218 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, on one MI350P (gfx950), over the five files in the command above: `tests/kernels/test_rocm_aiter_rmsnorm_mxfp4_quant.py` 49, `tests/compile/passes/test_rocm_aiter_mxfp4_norm_fusion.py` 81, `tests/compile/passes/test_rocm_aiter_mxfp4_fusion_gating.py` 56, `tests/compile/passes/test_vllm_fusion_pattern_matcher_pass.py` 8, `tests/compile/passes/test_rocm_aiter_act_mul_mxfp4_fusion.py` (#59153) 24. Run from this branch, 7 commits on main `56e3b081a`, mounted read-only into the pinned image (digest under Measurements) with the image's compiled extensions, not from a fresh build of vLLM. AITER 0.1.24.post1 (`amd-aiter`), `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` and `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4_ASM_GEMM=1`, one file per pytest run |

One is new and is in #59153's `MatcherGeluAndMul` (`matcher_utils.py`, return type); one that main has is fixed by #59153's fake signature |

No traceback and no eager fallback in the log. With act fusion also on: 64 act sites on `backbone`, 0 on `eagle_head` |

The measured checkpoint is `amd/Qwen3.8-27B-Quark-AWQ-MXFP4` with its `config.json` edited: eight module names of the MTP head were added to the end of the `quantization_config.exclude` list, so those modules are excluded from quantization. The names are `mtp.fc`, `mtp.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj`, `mtp.layers.0.self_attn.k_proj`, `mtp.layers.0.self_attn.v_proj`, `mtp.layers.0.self_attn.o_proj`, `mtp.layers.0.mlp.gate_proj`, `mtp.layers.0.mlp.up_proj` and `mtp.layers.0.mlp.down_proj`. Reproduce the end-to-end run (one gfx950 card):

```bash

vllm serve <checkpoint dir> --served-model-name amd/Qwen3.8-27B-Quark-AWQ-MXFP4 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.88 --max-model-len 60000 --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --kv-cache-dtype auto --enable-prefix-caching \
```

## Details

**The fusion.** On the asm path the MXFP4 linear quantizes its input inside the `gemm_with_dynamic_quant` custom op, so Inductor cannot fuse the norm into it. The new op `rocm_aiter_rmsnorm_mxfp4_quant(x, residual, weight, epsilon)` calls AITER's `add_rmsnorm_quant` and returns the MXFP4 codes, the shuffled e8m0 scales and the residual output; the GEMM takes the codes and scales through its existing `x_scales` argument. The pass `RocmAiterRMSNormMxfp4GemmFusionPass` rewrites `fused_add_rms_norm -> gemm_with_dynamic_quant` (asm path) into the op plus that GEMM(s). It is built once per enabled flag: `sites="post"` takes the post-attention norm of each decoder layer (one GEMM, gate_up), `sites="input"` takes the input norm that starts a layer, so each flag is judged and logged on its own and both flags together give two passes. The two kinds look the same by shape; the pass tells them apart by where the residual comes from, which needs the graph split at the attention ops, and refuses to be built without that split.

**The shared quantization.** An input norm feeds one GEMM in a full-attention layer (`qkv_proj`) and two in a gated delta net layer (`in_proj_qkvz`, `in_proj_ba`). The pattern matcher cannot match a norm whose output has users beyond the pattern's, so the input pass registers a second pattern, `AiterAddRMSNormMxfp4GemmPairPattern`, for two GEMMs: one fused op, and both GEMMs take its codes and scales through `x_scales`. A site is fused for all of its consumers or for none: a norm with a third GEMM, a reader that is not a GEMM, or one GEMM that is ineligible (below) is left whole. The pair pattern has two GEMM slots; the matcher can bind both to the same GEMM depending on the order in which the graph lists the users, so `extra_check` refuses that match and the matcher goes on to the real pair (a test lists the users both ways). The pass uuid includes the site kind, so the compile cache never serves one kind's graph for the other.

**What the pass refuses, at match time** (the op's fake raises on what it cannot take, so these must not reach it): tensor parallel size above 1, hidden size not a multiple of 32 or above 8192, non-bf16 or non-2D inputs, and a GEMM weight shape (of any GEMM of the site) with a tuned Triton preshuffle config (that GEMM may take a small-M branch that reads unshuffled scales; the op writes the asm layout). The op's argument contract is one pure function, `rocm_aiter_rmsnorm_mxfp4_quant_args_error`, used by the op, its fake and the pass.

**Start-up check.** `TargetGraphSiteCheckMixin` counts rewritten sites per compile range (the first piece of a model has no site, so nothing is judged per piece). `PostGradPassManager.finish_compile`, called by `VllmBackend` after the last piece and before the compile cache index is saved, makes the pass judge the whole graph: a target model graph in which the pass ran for a compile range and rewrote nothing fails the start, naming the flag; speculative decoding graphs (`is_target_model_graph`, e.g. the bf16 MTP head) are only logged. If the pass never ran because Inductor served every piece from its cache, a warning is logged. The backend hands the graph name to the pass manager as an attribute and calls `finish_compile` only if the pass manager has it, so a platform's own pass manager (`get_pass_manager_cls`) keeps working unchanged. N in the log line counts the sites in the pieces the pass ran on; vLLM compiles identical pieces once.

**Small shared changes.** `VllmPatternReplacement.extra_check` (default accepts everything) is forwarded by `VllmFusionPatternMatcherPass.register`, so a replacement can refuse a match; existing replacements are unaffected. The fake of `gemm_with_dynamic_quant` takes its arguments in the real op's order (already in #59153; a test pins it, because passing `x_scales` and `out_dtype` positionally depends on it).

**Limits.** gfx950 asm MXFP4 path only; tensor parallel 1; Gemma-style norm (the kernel adds 1 to the weight). Not covered: the gated RMSNorm inside a gated delta net (the subject of #59553), and layer 0's norm, which is a plain `rms_norm` with no residual. Size: about 820 lines of source on top of #59153 (the op and its contract 180, the passes and the start-up check 555, wiring and flags 86) and about 2650 lines of tests, most of them on fake tensors; I can split it: the op and its contract, then the post-attention pass and the start-up check, then the input pass and the pair pattern. Expected to work on any gfx950 (MI350X, MI355X, MI350P); tested only on MI350P (128 CU). On 256-CU parts, AITER's shipped tuned tables route some GEMM shapes to the Triton preshuffle path, which the pass refuses, so fewer sites may fuse there. Open PRs that would change these figures if they land first: #58139 routes 96-row scale tiles (the GDN `in_proj_ba` GEMM) to Triton, so the 47 GDN input-norm sites would stay unfused and the 63-site and launch-count figures would drop; #61278 removes `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4_ASM_GEMM`, which the commands above set. I will update this PR if either merges first.

+class ActMulMxfp4Model(torch.nn.Module):
+    """act_and_mul feeding an MXFP4 weight through the AITER ASM GEMM op."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        act: torch.nn.Module,
+        hidden_size: int,
+        dtype: torch.dtype,
+        use_asm_gemm: bool,
+    ):
+        super().__init__()
+        import aiter
+        from aiter.ops.shuffle import shuffle_weight
+
+        self.act = act
+        self.dtype = dtype
+        self.use_asm_gemm = use_asm_gemm
+        w = torch.randn(hidden_size, hidden_size, dtype=dtype) * 0.02
+        self.w_ref = w
+        w_q, w_s = aiter.per_1x32_f4_quant_hip(w, shuffle=False)
+        w_q, w_s = w_q.view(torch.uint8), w_s.view(torch.uint8)
+        # The layouts AiterMxfp4LinearKernel.process_weights_after_loading
+        # produces for each GEMM path.
+        if use_asm_gemm:
+            sm, sn = w_s.shape

+        self.weight_scale = torch.nn.Parameter(w_s, requires_grad=False)

+        if act_name == "silu":

+        else:
+            approximate = "tanh" if act_name == "gelu_tanh" else "none"
+            h = torch.nn.functional.gelu(gate, approximate=approximate) * up
+        return h @ self.w_ref.float().T
+

+        y = self.act(x)
+        return torch.ops.vllm.gemm_with_dynamic_quant(

+# --- the input site kind: the norm that starts a decoder layer ---------------------
+#
+# An input norm takes the residual the previous layer's post-attention norm returned
+# (see _norm_site_kind). A full-attention layer has ONE GEMM on its output (qkv_proj),
+# a gated delta net layer TWO (in_proj_qkvz and in_proj_ba), and the input pass
+# quantizes once and gives the codes and scales to every GEMM. Layer 0's norm is a
+# plain rms_norm with no residual and is never a site.
+
+
+def _input_site(x, residual, w, w2, wq, ws):
+    """The next layer's input norm and ONE GEMM (a full-attention layer's qkv_proj).
+
+    A norm with no GEMM after it stands in for the post-attention norm: the input norm
+    takes its residual output, which is what makes the second norm an input norm.
+    """
+    y, residual_out = _norm(x, residual, w)
+    y2, residual_out2 = _norm(y, residual_out, w2)
+    return _gemm(y2, wq, ws), residual_out2
+
+
+def _input_pair_site(x, residual, w, w2, wq, ws, wq_ba, ws_ba):
+    """An input norm and TWO GEMMs: in_proj_qkvz (the n of _trace), in_proj_ba (96)."""
+    y, residual_out = _norm(x, residual, w)
+    y2, residual_out2 = _norm(y, residual_out, w2)
+    return _gemm(y2, wq, ws), _gemm(y2, wq_ba, ws_ba), residual_out2
+
+
+def _input_site_also_read(x, residual, w, w2, wq, ws):
+    """An input norm whose output feeds a GEMM and something that is not a GEMM."""
+    y, residual_out = _norm(x, residual, w)
+    y2, residual_out2 = _norm(y, residual_out, w2)
+    return _gemm(y2, wq, ws), y2 * 2.0, residual_out2
+
+
+def _input_pair_site_also_read(x, residual, w, w2, wq, ws, wq_ba, ws_ba):
+    """The pair of GEMMs of _input_pair_site and a third reader that is not a GEMM."""
+    y, residual_out = _norm(x, residual, w)
+    y2, residual_out2 = _norm(y, residual_out, w2)
+    return _gemm(y2, wq, ws), _gemm(y2, wq_ba, ws_ba), y2 * 2.0, residual_out2

+def _gemm_weight_widths(graph):

+def _output_gemm_widths(graph, count=2):
+    """The N of the weight of each of the first `count` outputs of a piece, in order.

+    output of the piece: a rewrite that returned the right values in the wrong slots
